Image from Pixabay

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock returned 193.4% in the year to October 12, 2026, far outpacing the 20.5% return for the S&P 500. The company's sales growth sped up over those twelve months, and management raised its outlook for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 on September 2, 2026. On September 30, it raised its long-term growth forecast for its networking business and announced a $1.2 billion AI order from cloud firm Vultr. So how much has the business itself grown over that year?

How Quickly Is HPE's Revenue Rising?

Sales over the last twelve months reached $41.9 billion, up 26.6% from $33.1 billion a year earlier. Revenue in fiscal Q3 2026 reached a record $12.2 billion. That figure was up 34% from a year earlier, management noted during the September 2, 2026 call. Just three quarters before that, sales were growing 14.4%. Unlike the order figure below, these growth rates are not adjusted for the acquired Juniper Networks.

Server revenue grew 35% in fiscal Q3 2026. Management stated that higher selling prices on traditional servers drove the increase, while supply limits restricted the total number of servers HPE could ship. AI systems brought in almost $1.6 billion of that quarter's sales.

What Does HPE Stock Cost Against Its Sales Now?

HPE stock currently costs 2.2 times the company's sales over the last twelve months. That multiple had stayed between 0.4 and 1.4 over the past ten years. The share price rose far faster than sales did, so buyers now pay more for each dollar of HPE's revenue than they did in any of those years. On earnings, the stock is priced at 33.7 times.

The stock price appears to assume sales will keep growing, and management is forecasting exactly that. The company expects fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion, which is above the record it reported for Q3. Management now expects revenue to grow 13% to 17% for fiscal 2027. Orders grew 42% in fiscal Q3 2026, calculated on a basis that counts the acquired Juniper Networks in both years. Furthermore, HPE ended the quarter with a record backlog.

HPE's Margin Is Back At 7.8%

HPE kept 7.8% of its sales as operating profit over the last twelve months. This matches the 7.8% it kept two years ago. The margin fell to 6.2% a year ago and has since recovered, yet it remains below the 8.8% recorded three years ago. It is also far below the 18.5% posted by the S&P 500.

Management stated on the September 2, 2026 call that it expects its adjusted operating margin, which runs well above the 7.8% figure, to decline from the previous quarter. The company named a larger share of AI systems in what it sells among the reasons for this expected drop. The adjusted operating margin is the number to watch when the company reports fiscal Q4 2026.

title: Here is What to Know Beyond Why Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI) is a Trending Stock

Here is What to Know Beyond Why Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI) is a Trending Stock

Trade SMCI on Coinbase

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this server technology company have returned +8.8%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +2.1% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry, which Super Micro falls in, has lost 10.7%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Super Micro is expected to post earnings of $1.06 per share, indicating a change of +202.9% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1.1% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $4.37 points to a change of +20.4% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.13 indicates a change of +17.5% from what Super Micro is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Super Micro.

Why Super Micro (SMCI) Stock Is Nosediving
What Happened?

Shares of server solutions provider Super Micro (NASDAQ:SMCI) fell 5.5% in the afternoon session after reports indicated that a former contractor admitted to conspiring with a company co-founder to illegally export restricted artificial intelligence technology to China. According to Tipranks, contractor Ting-Wei Sun pleaded guilty Thursday in Manhattan federal court to four counts, including conspiracies to break export rules, smuggle goods, defraud the United States, and obstruct justice. Prosecutors charged him in March, along with co-founder Yih-Shyan Liaw and a Taiwan sales manager, with a scheme that began around October 2023 to send about $2.5 billion of U.S. artificial-intelligence servers to China without licenses. The indictment covers servers built with Nvidia's B200, H100, and H200 chips. Bloomberg reported that Liaw has pleaded not guilty. According to TipRanks, the shares are also still working through a $7 billion equity offering, and the drop lined up with wider selling in artificial-intelligence stocks after questions about OpenAI's revenue figures.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy Super Micro? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What Is The Market Telling Us

Super Micro's shares are extremely volatile and have had 66 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 10 days ago when the stock gained 4.3% on the news that the company began shipping server racks built for NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin AI architecture, according to TipRanks. The start of shipments reinforces SMCI's role in the AI infrastructure supply chain. Vera Rubin–ready racks house and interconnect high-density systems that data centers need for advanced AI workloads, keeping the stock in the AI server buildout story.

Super Micro is up 26.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $39.30 per share, it is still trading 28.6% below its 52-week high of $55.04 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Super Micro's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $10,952.

title: Did The Market Read Super Micro Computer Stock Right?
detail:
Did The Market Read Super Micro Computer Stock Right?
Trefis Team

SMCI

DELL
HPE
ANET
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Shares of Super Micro Computer (SMCI) returned 65.7% between April 12 and October 9, 2026, easily outpacing the 15.2% gain for the S&P 500. Most of that rally occurred during the final three months of the period, a stretch that featured the company's August 11 quarterly update following an earlier release in early May. The August report included executive projections for significantly higher sales, though those forecasts are not results yet. So what did Super Micro tell investors in those two reports?

What Super Micro Told Investors In May And August

In early May, Super Micro posted fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $10.24 billion, climbing 123% from a year earlier. The company also saw its adjusted gross margin recover to 10.1%. Shares climbed in extended trade once executives delivered an outlook for fiscal Q4 2026 that beat expectations.

During the August 11 call, executives detailed fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $11.1 billion, a 93% increase from a year earlier. Super Micro also secured more than $60 billion of new orders in that single quarter, pushing its backlog to a record level.

Super Micro was not alone in its rally, however, and the stock actually rose far less than two other server makers over the same six months. Dell Technologies and Hewlett Packard Enterprise each returned more than 190%, suggesting buyers were paying up for server makers as a group.

How High Is Super Micro Guiding For Fiscal 2027?

On the August 11 call, executives provided fiscal 2027 sales guidance of $65 billion to $72 billion. Super Micro generated $39.1 billion in sales over the last twelve months, meaning the low end of that new forecast is about two-thirds higher.

Server and storage systems accounted for 97% of its fiscal 2025 revenue, meaning the forecast covers nearly everything Super Micro sells.

The company came close to missing its previous forecast, however. Revenue for fiscal Q4 2026 landed near the low end of management's own guide. Executives blamed the result on short-term delays at customers whose power and cooling were not ready, and they expect to recognize that revenue in later quarters.

Super Micro Still Makes Little On Each Server Sold

Super Micro's gross margin, which measures the share of sales left after the cost of building its systems, was 10.8% over the last twelve months. That figure stood at 18.0% three years ago, and it has been lower in each twelve-month period since.

The fiscal Q4 2026 margin looked much better, reaching 17.6% on the adjusted measure. Executives noted that about 75% of the 750 basis point improvement from the quarter before came from a better customer and product mix. The remaining 25% came from lower tariff costs and lower inventory reserves, which the company called perhaps a one-time benefit.

Super Micro (SMCI) Upgraded to Strong Buy: Here's What You Should Know

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) appears an attractive pick, as it has been recently upgraded to a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). An upward trend in earnings estimates -- one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices -- has triggered this rating change.

The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.

The power of a changing earnings picture in determining near-term stock price movements makes the Zacks rating system highly useful for individual investors, since it can be difficult to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts. These are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time.

Therefore, the Zacks rating upgrade for Super Micro basically reflects positivity about its earnings outlook that could translate into buying pressure and an increase in its stock price.

Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices

The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, has proven to be strongly correlated with the near-term price movement of its stock. The influence of institutional investors has a partial contribution to this relationship, as these big professionals use earnings and earnings estimates to calculate the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.

For Super Micro, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade fundamentally mean an improvement in the company's underlying business. And investors' appreciation of this improving business trend should push the stock higher.

Harnessing the Power of Earnings Estimate Revisions

As empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock movements, tracking such revisions for making an investment decision could be truly rewarding. Here is where the tried-and-tested Zacks Rank stock-rating system plays an important role, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.

The Zacks Rank stock-rating system, which uses four factors related to earnings estimates to classify stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), has an impressive externally-audited track record, with Zacks Rank #1 stocks generating an average annual return of +25% since 1988.
